c.tagline: Scotland's warm-hearted second city — Victorian grandeur, music, and legendary nightlife.

taxi.fareNote: Licensed black hackney cabs are metered and can be hailed on the street; private-hire cars (including Uber and Bolt) must be pre-booked through the app.

emergency.note: 112 also works and connects to police, fire, and ambulance.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Very safe centrally; caution in some East End areas at night

hood_desc: The commercial and cultural core around George Square, Buchanan Street and the 'Style Mile' of shops, with grand Victorian buildings, theatres and the two main rail stations; best for first-timers who want everything on the doorstep.
A stylish grid of converted 18th-century warehouses just east of the centre, packed with bars, restaurants, boutiques and the Gallery of Modern Art; lively day and night and popular for going out.

Glasgow's leafy, bohemian quarter around Byres Road and cobbled Ashton Lane, home to the University of Glasgow, Kelvingrove Art Gallery and the Botanic Gardens; full of cafes, bookshops and student energy.
A former industrial strip by the Clyde reborn as the city's hippest food-and-drink destination, with acclaimed restaurants and cocktail bars along Argyle Street next to the SEC and OVO Hydro.
A relaxed, residential swathe south of the river taking in Shawlands, Queen's Park and Pollok Country Park (with the Burrell Collection); quieter and more local, good for a calmer base.
lodging: Hotel du Vin at One Devonshire Gardens

water.note: Tap water is excellent, soft Highland-sourced and safe everywhere.

transit.pay: The SPT Subway uses a contactless Bramble smartcard or paper tickets from station machines (a single is about £1.75, a day ticket around £4.40). Buses take contactless bank cards or exact cash on board with a First Bus daily fare cap, and ScotRail suburban trains are paid at station machines or via the app.
transit.hours: The Subway runs roughly 6:30am-11:30pm (Sundays about 10am-6:15pm); First Bus night services and ScotRail trains cover the wider city into the late evening.
transit.note: Glasgow's SPT Subway is a small 15-station loop (the 'Clockwork Orange') circling the city centre and West End; the dense ScotRail suburban rail network and First buses reach everywhere else.

transit.m: Glasgow Airport Express bus 500 to Buchanan Bus Station, ~15-25 min, up to every 10 min, 24/7
Local bus 77 to the city centre (cheaper, slower)
